podcast.body: A solo version of "You Don't Bring Me Flowers" appeared on Neil Diamond's 1977 album "I'm Glad You're Here With Me Tonight." The following year, a duet version with Barbra Streisand would achieve a number one hit. "By the way, that album also has a solo version of You Don't Bring Me Flowers."

srcs.episode: Ep. 39 - American Top 40 - Keeping Our Feet on the Ground and Reaching for the Stars (Part 1)

podcast.body: After Gary Guthrie's spliced-together version became a radio phenomenon, Neil Diamond and Barbra Streisand went into a studio together to re-record "You Don't Bring Me Flowers" as an official "nose-to-nose duet." This re-recorded version became a number one hit on Billboard's Hot 100 in December 1978. "They went into a studio together, and re-recorded flowers as an actual nose-to-nose duet."

podcast.body: Neil Diamond co-wrote this song, a lament for a fading romance, and included his version on his own LP in 1978. It was an album cut and not released as a standalone single. "But flowers, a lament for a fading romance that Neil Diamond himself co-wrote, wasn't issued as a single by him or by Barbara Streisand."
